subject: math
title: Volume of Rectangular Prisms
seo_title: Grade 5 Volume Worksheets: Unit Cubes, V = l × w × h, Missing Edges and Two-Prism Solids
standard_text: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement. Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and improvised units. Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real world and mathematical problems involving volume. Apply the formulas V = l × w × h and V = b × h for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems. Recognize volume as additive. Find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 volume worksheets: count unit cubes, use V = l × w × h and V = B × h, find a missing edge, add the volumes of two prisms, and solve real-world word problems in cubic units. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Volume = length × width × height (V = l × w × h).
key_sub: Volume counts the unit cubes that fill a solid: cubes in one layer × number of layers. It is in cubic units (cu cm, cu ft). For two prisms put together, find each volume and add.
body_html:
What volume means

Volume is the amount of space inside a solid. We measure it by counting how many unit cubes fill the solid with no gaps and no overlaps. A cube with 1 cm edges is 1 cubic centimeter.

The two formulas

V = l × w × h (length × width × height). V = B × h, where B is the area of the base. Both say the same thing: cubes in one layer × number of layers.

Find a missing edge

A box has a volume of 120 cu in. It is 5 in long and 4 in wide. How tall is it?

5 × 4 × h = 120, so 20 × h = 120. 120 ÷ 20 = 6.

Answer: 6 in

Two prisms put together

Volume is additive. Split the solid into two rectangular prisms that do not overlap, find each volume, then add.

Units

MeasureUnitExample
Length (1 edge)cm, in, ft, m5 cm
Area (a flat face)sq cm, sq in, sq ft24 sq cm
Volume (space inside)cu cm, cu in, cu ft, cu m120 cu cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting only the cubes you can seeCount one layer, then multiply by the number of layers
Adding the edges: 6 + 4 + 5 = 15Multiply them: 6 × 4 × 5 = 120
Stopping at one face: 6 × 4 = 24That is the base. Multiply by the height, too
Writing sq cm for a volumeVolume is in cubic units: cu cm
Measuring prism B down to the floorUse only B's own height, so no part is counted twice

faq.q: What is the formula for the volume of a rectangular prism?
faq.a: V = l × w × h (length × width × height), or V = B × h, where B is the area of the base. The answer is in cubic units, such as cu cm or cu ft.

faq.q: How do you teach volume to 5th graders?
faq.a: Start by filling a box with unit cubes: count the cubes in one layer, then multiply by the number of layers. Then show that this is the same as l × w × h.

faq.q: How do you find the volume of a shape made of two rectangular prisms?
faq.a: Split it into two prisms that do not overlap, find the volume of each one with l × w × h, and add the two volumes.

faq.q: Why is volume measured in cubic units?
faq.a: Volume counts how many cubes fill a solid, and each cube has length, width and height. So 1 cubic inch is a cube with 1-inch edges.

items.q: The layers of this prism are pulled apart. How many unit cubes are in the whole prism?
items.e: One layer: 4 × 3 = 12 cubes. 2 layers: 12 × 2 = 24 cubes.

items.q: The bottom layer of a tray has 6 rows of 5 unit cubes. The tray holds 2 layers. How many unit cubes fill it?
items.e: One layer: 6 × 5 = 30 cubes. 2 layers: 30 × 2 = 60 cubes.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cubic unit. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: Each layer has 2 rows of 2 cubes = 4 cubes. There are 4 layers: 4 × 4 = 16 cubic units. Count the cubes you cannot see, too (only 13 cubes show a face).

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cubic unit. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: Each layer has 3 rows of 3 cubes = 9 cubes. There are 4 layers: 9 × 4 = 36 cubic units. Count the cubes you cannot see, too (only 24 cubes show a face).

sets.title: Use V = l × w × h and V = B × h

items.q: A cube has edges that are 9 in long. What is its volume?
items.e: Every edge of a cube is 9 in, so V = 9 × 9 × 9 = 81 × 9 = 729 cu in.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 15 × 9 × 5 = 135 × 5 = 675 cu in. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu in.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 15 × 7 × 10 = 105 × 10 = 1,050 cu ft. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu ft.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 13 × 8 × 6 = 104 × 6 = 624 cu m. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu m.

items.q: A cube has edges that are 11 m long. What is its volume?
items.e: Every edge of a cube is 11 m, so V = 11 × 11 × 11 = 121 × 11 = 1,331 cu m.

items.q: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of 48 sq m. The prism is 9 m tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = B × h, where B is the area of the base: 48 × 9 = 432 cu m. Think of 9 layers with 48 cubes in each.

items.e: Volume = length × width × height = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cubic centimeters.

items.e: V = l × w × h = 14 × 6 × 12 = 84 × 12 = 1,008 cu ft. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu ft.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 11 × 9 × 7 = 99 × 7 = 693 cu in. Volume uses all 3 edges, and the unit is cubic: cu in.

items.e: V = B × h, where B is the area of the base: 15 × 12 = 180 cu cm. Think of 12 layers with 15 cubes in each.

sets.title: Add the volumes of two prisms

items.q: This solid is made of unit cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: Bottom prism: 5 × 3 × 1 = 15 cubes. Top prism: 2 × 3 × 3 = 18 cubes. 15 + 18 = 33 cubic units. Count the hidden cubes, too.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 7 × 5 × 5 = 175. Prism B: 4 × 5 × 2 = 40. Add: 175 + 40 = 215 cu cm. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 2, not 7.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 11 × 5 × 2 = 110. Prism B: 8 × 5 × 5 = 200. Add: 110 + 200 = 310 cu cm. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 5, not 7.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 6 × 4 × 4 = 96. Prism B: 3 × 4 × 6 = 72. Add: 96 + 72 = 168 cu ft. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 6, not 10.

items.q: A storage shed has two parts shaped like rectangular prisms. One part is 10 ft by 6 ft by 4 ft. The other part is 6 ft by 6 ft by 5 ft. What is the total volume?
items.e: First part: 10 × 6 × 4 = 240. Second part: 6 × 6 × 5 = 180. Add: 240 + 180 = 420 cu ft.

items.q: This solid is made of unit cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: Bottom prism: 4 × 3 × 1 = 12 cubes. Top prism: 2 × 3 × 2 = 12 cubes. 12 + 12 = 24 cubic units. Count the hidden cubes, too.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 11 × 4 × 2 = 88. Prism B: 2 × 4 × 3 = 24. Add: 88 + 24 = 112 cu ft. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 3, not 5.

items.q: This solid is made of unit cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: Bottom prism: 4 × 3 × 3 = 36 cubes. Top prism: 2 × 3 × 2 = 12 cubes. 36 + 12 = 48 cubic units. Count the hidden cubes, too.

items.q: A set of concrete steps is made of two rectangular prisms. One part is 8 m by 3 m by 2 m. The other part is 3 m by 3 m by 4 m. What is the total volume?
items.e: First part: 8 × 3 × 2 = 48. Second part: 3 × 3 × 4 = 36. Add: 48 + 36 = 84 cu m.

items.q: Which expression gives the volume of this solid?
items.e: Prism A: 6 × 5 × 5 = 150. Prism B: 2 × 5 × 3 = 30. Add: 150 + 30 = 180 cu ft. Each prism needs all 3 of its own edges, and B is only 3 ft tall.

items.q: A model building has two parts shaped like rectangular prisms. One part is 12 cm by 9 cm by 7 cm. The other part is 8 cm by 5 cm by 7 cm. What is the total volume?
items.e: First part: 12 × 9 × 7 = 756. Second part: 8 × 5 × 7 = 280. Add: 756 + 280 = 1,036 cu cm.

items.q: Two wooden blocks are glued together to make a toy. One part is 5 in by 4 in by 3 in. The other part is 2 in by 4 in by 6 in. What is the total volume?
items.e: First part: 5 × 4 × 3 = 60. Second part: 2 × 4 × 6 = 48. Add: 60 + 48 = 108 cu in.

items.q: This solid is made of unit cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: Bottom prism: 5 × 2 × 3 = 30 cubes. Top prism: 3 × 2 × 2 = 12 cubes. 30 + 12 = 42 cubic units. Count the hidden cubes, too.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 7 × 4 × 3 = 84. Prism B: 5 × 4 × 5 = 100. Add: 84 + 100 = 184 cu in. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 5, not 8.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 11 × 2 × 4 = 88. Prism B: 6 × 2 × 3 = 36. Add: 88 + 36 = 124 cu in. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 3, not 7.

items.q: Which expression gives the volume of this solid?
items.e: Prism A: 7 × 2 × 4 = 56. Prism B: 3 × 2 × 2 = 12. Add: 56 + 12 = 68 cu cm. Each prism needs all 3 of its own edges, and B is only 2 cm tall.

items.q: Grace builds a solid from two rectangular prisms. The total volume is 150 cu cm. Prism A has a volume of 90 cu cm. Prism B is 5 cm long and 3 cm wide. How tall is prism B?
items.e: Prism B: 150 − 90 = 60 cu cm. Then 5 × 3 × h = 60, so 15 × h = 60 and h = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 cm.

items.q: Leo builds a solid from two rectangular prisms. The total volume is 200 cu in. Prism A has a volume of 120 cu in. Prism B is 4 in long and 5 in wide. How tall is prism B?
items.e: Prism B: 200 − 120 = 80 cu in. Then 4 × 5 × h = 80, so 20 × h = 80 and h = 80 ÷ 20 = 4 in.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 9 × 3 × 2 = 54. Prism B: 6 × 3 × 5 = 90. Add: 54 + 90 = 144 cu m. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 5, not 7.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms, A and B. What is its total volume?
items.e: Prism A: 8 × 2 × 2 = 32. Prism B: 6 × 2 × 3 = 36. Add: 32 + 36 = 68 cu m. Prism B starts on top of A, so its height is 3, not 5.

items.q: A brick is 8 in long, 4 in wide and 2 in tall. What is the total volume of 10 bricks?
items.e: One brick: 8 × 4 × 2 = 64 cu in. Ten bricks: 64 × 10 = 640 cu in.

items.q: Ava packs cubes with 2-inch edges into a box that is 8 in long, 6 in wide and 4 in tall. How many cubes fit?
items.e: Along each edge: 8 ÷ 2 = 4, 6 ÷ 2 = 3, 4 ÷ 2 = 2. Cubes: 4 × 3 × 2 = 24. (192 would be 1-inch cubes.)

items.q: A swimming pool is 25 m long and 10 m wide. The water is 2 m deep everywhere. How much water is in the pool?
items.e: V = 25 × 10 × 2 = 250 × 2 = 500 cu m. 250 is only the area of the pool.

items.q: Lily's aquarium is 20 inches long, 10 inches wide and 12 inches tall. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 20 × 10 × 12 = 200 × 12 = 2,400 cu in. 200 is only the area of the bottom.

items.q: Each layer of cubes in a box has 15 cubes. The box holds 90 cubes when it is full. How many layers are there?
items.e: Layers × cubes in each layer = total, so ? × 15 = 90. 90 ÷ 15 = 6 layers.

items.q: Ruby's toy chest is 3 ft long, 2 ft wide and 2 ft tall. How much space is inside it?
A fish tank is 30 cm long, 20 cm wide and 25 cm tall. Water fills it to a height of 20 cm. What is the volume of the water?
items.e: Use the height of the water, not the tank: 30 × 20 × 20 = 600 × 20 = 12,000 cu cm.

items.q: Storage unit A is 10 ft by 10 ft by 8 ft. Storage unit B is 12 ft by 8 ft by 8 ft. Which holds more, and how much more?
items.e: A: 10 × 10 × 8 = 800 cu ft. B: 12 × 8 × 8 = 768 cu ft. 800 − 768 = 32 cu ft. (Adding the edges gives 28 for both, but that is not volume.)

items.q: Kai fills a sandbox that is 6 feet long and 5 feet wide with sand 2 feet deep. How many cubic feet of sand does he need?
items.e: V = 6 × 5 × 2 = 30 × 2 = 60 cu ft. The depth of the sand is the height.

items.q: A box is 4 in long, 3 in wide and 5 in tall. A second box has the same base but is twice as tall. What is the volume of the second box?
items.e: The second box is 4 × 3 × 10 = 120 cu in. Doubling the height doubles the volume: 2 × 60 = 120. (480 would double every edge.)

items.q: A moving box holds 3,000 cubic inches. It is 20 inches long and 15 inches wide. How tall is it?
Box A is 6 cm by 5 cm by 4 cm. Box B is a cube with 5 cm edges. Which has the greater volume?
items.e: A: 6 × 5 × 4 = 120 cu cm. B: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 cu cm. B is greater by 125 − 120 = 5 cu cm.

items.q: Which unit could be used to measure the volume of a swimming pool?
items.e: Volume is the space inside a solid, so it uses cubic units. Square meters measure area, meters measure length, and kilograms measure mass.

items.q: A garden bed is made of two rectangular prisms. One is 6 ft by 3 ft by 2 ft. The other is 3 ft by 3 ft by 2 ft. How much soil fills the bed?
items.e: 6 × 3 × 2 = 36 and 3 × 3 × 2 = 18. Add the two parts: 36 + 18 = 54 cu ft.

items.q: A shipping container is 40 ft long, 8 ft wide and 8 ft tall. What is its volume?
Maya fills a sandbox that is 5 ft long, 4 ft wide and 1 ft deep. Sand costs $3 for each cubic foot. How much does the sand cost?
A cereal box is 8 inches wide, 3 inches deep and 12 inches tall. What is its volume?
Noah packs 1-foot cubes into a crate that is 4 feet long, 3 feet wide and 2 feet tall. How many cubes fit?
items.e: One layer: 4 × 3 = 12 cubes. 2 layers: 12 × 2 = 24 cubes, so the crate is 24 cu ft.

items.q: Emma stacks 3 boxes that are all the same. Each box is 12 in by 10 in by 6 in. What is the total volume of the 3 boxes?
items.e: One box: 12 × 10 × 6 = 720 cu in. Three boxes: 3 × 720 = 2,160 cu in.

items.q: Which of these could be the volume of a shoebox?
items.e: A volume is in cubic units, and a shoebox is about 12 in × 7 in × 5 in = 420 cu in. 600 cu ft would be bigger than a closet.
